statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration required beyond standard French conventions
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Reserved words such as 'État', 'République', 'Armée', 'Chambre de Commerce'; names infringing existing trademarks or similar to public entities; misleading or offensive terms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the greffe, file an administrative appeal to the Président du tribunal de commerce within 2 months; if denied, further recourse to administrative courts possible

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low likelihood (estimated 5-10%) of unannounced physical inspections for pre-incorporation verification by tax authorities or AML bodies

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (general provisions on commercial companies), L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL), R. 123-1 et seq. (RCS registration procedure); Regulation (EU) 852/2004 Art. 6 and Code rural et de la pêche maritime L. 233-1/2 for food-business declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the judicial district of the registered office; filings are transmitted electronically via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI portal, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création de société au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accompanied by the statuts constitutifs, certificat de dépôt des fonds, attestation de parution au Journal d'Annonces Légales, déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif, and the organs' acceptance documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital (Art. L. 223-2); capital is freely fixed by the statuts and can be as low as EUR 1. All shares must be fully subscribed. If capital is below EUR 10,000, the entire cash capital must be paid up at formation; if EUR 10,000 or more, at least 20% of each cash share must be released at subscription and the balance within 5 years. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked funds account (compte bloqué) with a French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary within 8 days; the certificate of deposit of funds (attestation de dépôt des fonds) is required for registration, and funds are released only upon issuance of the K-bis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole founding member of [Company] SARL hereby adopts the Articles of Association dated [date], subscribed fully; ALLOCATES the entire share capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] shares, all cash-subscribed and fully paid-up; FIXES the registered office at [address], within the jurisdiction of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de [city]; APPOINTS [Name] as Gérant for an indefinite term with the broadest powers to manage and represent the Company and to open bank accounts; DECLARES the beneficial owner; APPROVES the publication of the constitution notice; AUTHORIZES the Gérant to sign the incorporation file, deposit funds, publish the JAL notice, file the RBE declaration, and obtain the K-bis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and signing of the Articles of Association (Statuts) and acceptance of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders by private seal (sous seing privé) or by notarial act before a French Notaire (required for contributions of real property or goodwill).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the statuts in French: exact corporate name, legal form (SARL), duration (99 years), corporate purpose covering wholesale distribution of single-origin green Arabica coffee beans (NAF 4637Z / ISIC 4631), registered office, share capital, share allocation, shareholder identities, and identification of the Gérant. Have each shareholder sign every page and the final signature page; obtain the signed acceptance of office of the Gérant, his/her identity documents, proof of address, and declaration of non-condamnation (no criminal prohibition).
required_dossiers: Statuts constitutifs signed by all shareholders (original or certified copy)
Acceptance of office of the Gérant (acte de candidature)
Passport or national identity card of each shareholder and the Gérant
Proof of residential address of shareholders and Gérant
Déclaration de non-condamnation of the Gérant (no prohibition under Art. L. 223-4 C. com.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or counterparty requires a notarized form, convert the private-seal statuts into an authentic act by a notaire. Any omission in a shareholder's identity data is cured by a rectificative act signed by all members before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and blocking of cash capital contributions (Dépôt des fonds de capital)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank), Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC), or a Notaire acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked capital account in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the subscribed cash capital by SEPA/wire from each shareholder's bank account; for a SARL with capital below EUR 10,000, the full amount must be released immediately; for capital of EUR 10,000 or more, at least 20% must be paid up. The depositary issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds and blocks the funds until presentation of the K-bis; funds are then transferred to the company's operating account.
required_dossiers: Final signed statuts (brought to the depositary)
Identity documents of each subscriber
Wire-transfer or deposit evidence of the capital amount
Certificate of deposit of funds (attestation de dépôt des fonds) issued by the depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced AML/KYC due diligence on source of funds, provide supporting bank statements and source-of-wealth documents for shareholders. If the depositary refuses release after registration, present the K-bis and demand immediate release under Art. L. 223-7 C. com.; an unjustified refusal is actionable before the commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the constitution notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales admitted in the département of the registered office (authorized legal gazette); online JAL platforms are acceptable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the legal notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate purpose summarizing green coffee wholesale distribution, duration, identity of the Gérant, and the registry where the company will be registered. Submit to the selected JAL, pay the publication fee, and obtain the attestation de parution (publication receipt), which is mandatory for the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: JAL notice text approved by the shareholders/ Gérant
Proof of payment of the publication fee
Attestation de parution au JAL (official receipt of insertion)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains a factual error or is published prematurely before the statuts are final, publish a rectificatif in the same JAL and attach both attestations to the incorporation file. A delay in publication does not block the file if the attestation is obtained before submission; otherwise, the registry will issue a single query listing the missing piece.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the complete immatriculation dossier on the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), automatically routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office district.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the online account, select 'société commerciale – création', and complete the electronic declaration with the corporate data, shareholders, Gérant, registered office, and activity description aligned to ISIC 4631 / NAF 4637Z. Attach the signed statuts, certificate of deposit of funds, JAL attestation, declaration of the beneficial owner (RBE) with all required personal data, identity and address documents, and the registered-office accommodation proof. Pay the official registry fees online. The registry performs the legal control within 5 working days and issues the RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Electronic declaration of creation (M0-equivalent) on the INPI portal
Signed statuts constitutifs
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate)
Attestation de parution au Journal d'Annonces Légales
Déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif (RBE) with identity, nationality, address, and percentage of control
Identity documents (passport/ID) and proof of address of the Gérant and shareholders
Registered-office accommodation document (lease, title deed, or gratuitous accommodation agreement)
Declaration of no criminal conviction of the Gérant
If the Gérant is a non-EU national: valid residence permit or equivalent authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry must, within 5 working days, either register the company or issue a single written request listing all missing or irregular items, suspending the deadline until the cure. The applicant completes the file through the Guichet Unique. If the registry refuses registration or fails to act, the shareholder/Gérant may apply to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce for an order compelling registration (injonction de procéder under Art. R. 123-93 C. com.), or correct the RBE declaration and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the K-bis certificate and allocation of SIREN/SIRET identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (the greffier effects the RCS registration).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the legal control, the greffier registers the company in the RCS, allocates the SIREN (national identifier) and SIRET codes, transmits the data automatically to INSEE, DGFiP, and URSSAF, and issues the official extrait d'immatriculation au RCS (K-bis). The K-bis constitutes the legal proof of corporate existence. The blocked capital funds are then released to the company's operational account upon presentation of the K-bis.
required_dossiers: No additional dossiers are required by the applicant; the K-bis is issued directly by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis contains an error in corporate data, managers, or activity code, submit a rectification request (bordereau de régularisation) to the registry through the Guichet Unique. If registration is delayed beyond the legal 5-working-day period, serve a formal notice on the greffier and, failing action, request the presiding judge of the commercial court to order registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration activation of tax, VAT, social, and food-business registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP/SIE), INSEE, URSSAF, and Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail, des Solidarités et de la Protection des Populations (DDETSPP) via the GALEE teleservice of the DGCCRF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the K-bis, verify the automatic activation of the French intra-Community VAT number (FR + SIREN) at the local SIE and the corporate tax (impôt sur les sociétés) filing obligations. Register the company as a food business operator (exploitant du secteur alimentaire) by filing the déclaration d'activité sanitaire with the competent DDETSPP/DGCCRF at least 15 days before starting the green coffee wholesale operations. If the company hires staff, complete the employer registration with URSSAF. Open the operational commercial bank account and configure documentary credit and SWIFT rails for LC-backed coffee import payments.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-bis (RCS certificate)
Statuts constitutifs
SIREN/SIRET INSEE notification
Registered-office lease or title deed
Bank RIB (relevé d'identité bancaire) of the operational account
GALEE declaration form with complete activity description (NAF 4637Z, wholesale of green coffee)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the intra-Community VAT number is not activated, confirm the SIREN status with INSEE and file a written activation request with the SIE of the registered office. If the GALEE declaration is queried, correct the activity description (grossiste en café vert en grains, non torréfié) and re-file; the DDETSPP issues a récépissé upon acceptance. In case of discrepancy in the employer registration, rectify directly with URSSAF via the déclaration sociale des entreprises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF) acting through the Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail, des Solidarités et de la Protection des Populations (DDETSPP) of the department of the registered office; industrial site inspections under the DREAL for any classified installation (ICPE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'activité sanitaire de l'exploitant du secteur alimentaire (Registre des exploitants, Code rural et de la pêche maritime, Art. L. 233-1/2 and R. 233-1 et seq.), filed through the GALEE teleservice prior to commencing green coffee warehouse/distribution activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement - DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) / Mission Régionale d'Autorité Environnementale (MRAe) for case-by-case screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Case-by-case screening (examen au cas par cas); exempt from a full EIA where the storage volume of the coffee warehousing area is below 500 m³ (below the ICPE Rubrique 1510 threshold). If storage volume is between 500 m³ and 50,000 m³, the warehouse enters the ICPE declaration regime (régime de la déclaration) under the Ministerial Order of 11 April 2017, requiring a prior declaration and compliance monitoring, but not a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant industrial discharges for green coffee handling: wastewater limited to sanitary and cleaning water discharged to the municipal sewer with a local arrêté d'autorisation de rejet under Art. L. 1331-10 Code de l'environnement; negligible VOC/dust emissions, but if a mechanical dedusting or green-bean grading unit is installed, emission thresholds under Directive (EU) 2016/2284 and local arrêté préfectoral apply; waste sorting, traceability, and valorization obligations under Arts. L. 541-1 to L. 541-33 Code de l'environnement and the five-flow AGEC sorting decree; pest control and hygienic storage per Annex II of Regulation (EC) 852/2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Maintain a Registre de sécurité (fire-safety register) at the premises; annual verification of extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation lighting per Code du travail Arts. R. 4227-1 et seq.; complete a Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP) covering handling of jute/grain bags, forklift traffic, and dust; obtain Consuel certificates for electrical/gas installations and the DAA/DDT declaration of completion of works for any fit-out; if the premises are open to the public, ERP classification and fire-commission inspection apply; workplace medical clearance and safety training for all employees before the start of activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French Banking and Monetary Control) in cooperation with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the Ministère de l'Économie, and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking/banking conduct supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions (Article 63 TFEU) and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayments, and investment returns are freely transferable to non-residents without exchange-control approval. Real-world frictions: strict AML/KYC documentation, €12,500 individual cross-border transaction reporting threshold for the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics, and EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening. For a specialty green coffee importer, no special convertibility licence is required; the euro is the domestic currency and all commercial payments to non-EU coffee suppliers are treated as ordinary trade payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements in France. French exporters are not obliged to convert foreign currency receipts into euros, nor to repatriate them within a specific statutory timeline. However, all cross-border monetary transactions exceeding €12,500 (or equivalent) must be reported to the Banque de France as part of the balance-of-payments statistics via the EMTA (Entreprises de Montant Trimestriel) or single-transaction declaration system. The SARL may retain USD proceeds from third-country re-exports, but treasury efficiency is maximised by converting INR?/EUR/USD through approved banks with documented trade cover.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency current account (EUR/USD) with SWIFT Access
Operational current account in EUR with documentary LC and trade finance desk
Operational current account and capital escrow account (compte bloqué) for SARL incorporation deposits
Operational account for mid-size corporate import and mobility of funds
Basic operational account with limited trade finance products

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for routine payment initiation and FX conversion, Low for documentary trade finance. Regulated French EMIs (e.g. Qonto, Blackbird, Treezor) operate under an ACPR/DPG permit and can hold client funds in safeguarded accounts, but they are not credit institutions and cannot issue or confirm letters of credit or take term deposits. Therefore, Qonto/EMIs are suitable for operational EUR treasury and low-risk supplier payments, while the core of import settlement for specialty green coffee containers (especially origin-country confirmed LCs) must be executed through a tier-1 bank with an international correspondent network.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Traditional tier-1 French banks generally require the SARL manager (gérant) and any signatory shareholder to attend a face-to-face interview or visit the branch in person for initial account opening, particularly for non-resident directors. Remote opening using electronic identification (eIDAS-certified video identification) is possible for some products, but the bank retains the right to require physical appearance in cases of complex ownership, non-EEA shareholders, or the need to verify original incorporation documents. Fintech EMIs accept fully remote onboarding, but this reduces access to trade financing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or unfiled Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) at the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce; a legal condition for any bank account filing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide separate RBE certificate from the commercial court (registre), Articles of Association, original 'Kbis' extract (dated within 3 months), and proof of publication of the statutory declaration in a legal gazette.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner (BO) with opaque or high-risk source-of-wealth profile; bank demands explanation of the ultimate source of the funds to be used for capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate chain chart, passport, address proof of all ultimate beneficial owners, source-of-wealth declaration (e.g. leading foreign salary, share sale contracts, inheritance), bank reference letters, and audited financial statements of the parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hit on a shareholder or coffee-origin counterparty (e.g. non-EU producer payee with partial ownership by persons on restricted lists).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and negative-media screening reports, SWIFT payment case, origin/trade product contracts, phytosanitary certificates, pre/past shipment documents, and a written AML rationale confirming no designated person or entity is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of apparent economic substance: French SARL with a single foreign director and no local operations in the early stage; a shell-risk red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised office lease in France, employment contracts (if any), EBICS electronic banking mandate, storage/contractor agreements, purchase/sale agreements from the coffee trade, and documented physical stock inspection or warehouse receipts evidencing the commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank questionnaire requiring evidence of ‘précis de conformité’ for coffee sourcing under EU deforestation and commodity standards (EUDR) and sustainability requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Coffee traceability dossier including geolocation data of the coffee farms/origin parcels, supply-chain due-diligence policy, certifications (Rainforest Alliance, Organic, Fairtrade, CAFE), and accumulated contracts with origin exporter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital contributions via SWIFT MT103 in EUR or USD through a comptoir in the shareholder's jurisdiction to the SARL's French euro account. Use BIC/IBAN with TARGET2 Eurosystem clearing. For statutory incorporation: (a) open a temporary blocked account with the chosen bank; (b) file the capital deposit undertaking (attestation de blocage de fonds) in the Kbis/registration; (c) after Kbis issuance, the bank releases funds into the SARL operational account. Purpose code under French balance-of-payments: use ‘S001 – Equity capital on incorporation’ or equivalent nomenclature for non-resident direct investment share capital. If the capital contribution exceeds €12,500, submit the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration (EMTA or single transaction form) within the statutory period. The shareholder must document source of funds to avoid AML inquiries: notarised transfer deed, approved minutes of Shareholders’ Meeting, tax integrity certificate from the contributing entity, and bank reference letter.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For specialty green coffee bean container imports: (1) direct payment via SWIFT MT103 from the French bank to the origin-country exporter after presenting invoice, bill of lading, packing list, phytosanitary certificate, and 20-digit tariff code 0901.11; (2) stronger protection: irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (LC) issued by the French bank (SWIFT MT700) in favour of the exporter, with the exporter presenting documents through a confirming bank at origin; (3) trade loans or trust receipt financing at the custom’s arrival, using the SARL warehouse receipts as security. All outbound disbursements require a stated payment narrative matching customs invoices, and the bank must receive the BOP declaration for payments to non-residents > €12,500. In EUR, settlement is handled via TARGET2; in USD via the French bank’s correspondent USD account (e.g. through a New York clearer). LC confirmation costs and interest are borne by the import entity. No specific foreign-exchange permit is required for paying foreign coffee exporters, provided the payment is originated from legitimate documented trade.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward with a physical underlying coffee trade receivable/payable (standard plain-vanilla forward)
EUR/USD FX swap for rolling a funding leg into the next-month settlement when underlying LC payment is postponed
European-style EUR/USD currency option (purchase of calls/puts) for hedging an expected coffee-supplier payable while preserving upside from favourable EUR/USD movement
Cross-currency swap (FCY/EUR basis swap) for synchronising USD import payables with a USD-denominated financing deposit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels au registre du commerce et des sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end for shareholder approval; deposit with the registry within one month of approval and no later than seven months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the manager to an administrative fine of up to EUR 1,500, a court-ordered daily penalty (astreinte), the loss of legal opposability of accounts against third parties, and, after formal notice with unexplained non-compliance, administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, filing by 3 May of the following year; for other fiscal year-ends, filing within three months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of net tax due, increasing to 40% after a 30-day formal notice, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; failure may also trigger tax reassessment and enforced recovery against the company's assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local economic contribution – Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due by 15 December each year (or the next business day); for the first year of activity, a temporary rental-value declaration is generally due by 15 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalties of 5% plus 0.20% monthly interest; formal enforcement notice (mise en demeure) followed by garnishment or asset seizure; continued default may be borne personally by the legal representative if removal of assets is proven.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of corporate data and beneficial ownership record consistency (attached with annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual accounts deposit deadline; immediate update within 30 days if any beneficial-owner or registered-office change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or missing beneficial-owner data exposes the company to criminal fine of up to EUR 18,000 (EUR 90,000 for a legal person) and an administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000; persistent non-updated RCS data may trigger judicial injunction and strike-off procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed for an SARL if at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at fiscal year-end: balance-sheet total greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax greater than EUR 8,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Mandatory appointment may also be imposed by shareholders or by court if the company is part of a group controlling another entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG) under Articles L123-12 et seq. of the French Commercial Code is mandatory for the individual statutory accounts of an SARL; IFRS as adopted in the EU is permitted only for consolidated accounts of listed parent companies and is not applicable to the standalone SARL accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a standalone annual UBO declaration. The Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing is made at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership. Nevertheless, as part of the annual accounts filing and RCS renewal, the manager must verify the RBE record's accuracy; any share transfer or ownership change affecting this specialty-green-coffee import SARL must be re-filed with the Greffe within 30 days after the transfer closes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors' and Shareholders' Decisions (registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – USD 22,000 per year if mandatory audit thresholds are met; otherwise no audit fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, paid-in capital is fully paid, and at least 75% of capital and voting rights are held by individuals or qualifying entities. The standard 25% rate applies above the preferential band. Research, innovation, and investment incentives may reduce the effective burden but do not generally alter the headline rate. French tax losses are generally carried forward without a fixed expiry, subject to annual utilization limits; the first EUR 1 million plus 50% of the excess taxable profit may normally be offset in a year. The schema-specified five-year value is not the general French rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French Tax Administration professional portal (impots.gouv.fr, espace professionnel), with the electronic tax package generally comprising Forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD and Forms 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, as applicable. Form 2572-SD is used for the balance payment and Forms 2571-SD and 2572-SD may be used for installment and balance payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; corporate income tax installments are generally paid four times annually, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and tax package are generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second working day after 1 May of the following year. Electronic tax payment and the balance are generally due by the same statutory deadline, subject to the applicable French tax calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, principal activity, fiscal year dates, tax office, and status as a French SARL subject to corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the French permanent establishment or subsidiary identity separately from the foreign shareholder. Use the French entity's SIREN and French registered address; do not substitute the foreign parent's tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss transferred from the tax package, after French tax adjustments and utilization of eligible tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to the French company or French taxable presence. Foreign-owner income is not included unless legally attributable to the French entity or permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary additions and deductions, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation adjustments, provisions, exempt income, and tax-specific adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile intercompany charges, import costs, customs-related expenses, financing charges, and foreign exchange items to French accounting records and supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses generated in the year, losses utilized, and closing losses available for future periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual utilization cap and preserve evidence of the legal continuity of the SARL. Significant changes in activity or ownership can restrict loss utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2058-C-SD, tax credits and taxable profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after adjustments, tax credits, and relevant tax reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally available to the French company and retain certificates, payroll records, invoices, and qualifying expenditure schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2059-A-SD to 2059-G-SD, capital gains, provisions, depreciation, and balance-sheet tax schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of fixed assets, provisions, capital gains, depreciation, equity movements, and other tax-balance-sheet items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported green coffee inventory is generally trading stock rather than a depreciable asset. Reconcile customs valuation, freight, insurance, storage, foreign exchange, and inventory valuation to the general ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of applicable foreign-related-party transactions, participation interests, tax consolidation matters, and withholding-tax information where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign parent, sister companies, suppliers, lenders, licensors, and service providers. Maintain contracts, invoices, payment evidence, beneficial-owner information, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable after crediting installments, withholding taxes, and eligible tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that any foreign tax credit is legally creditable in France and that French withholding tax obligations on outbound payments have been separately reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installment amounts and payment references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's tax account and bank mandate. A foreign shareholder's payment does not replace the French company's filing or payment obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payment authorization, French tax account references, and bank details maintained in the professional portal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use an authorized representative or French bank payment arrangement where foreign management cannot access the French professional portal.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing in cases of formal notice, abuse, or fraudulent conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and reductions or exceptions. Material omissions, false information, or deliberate fraud can trigger penalties of 40% or 80%, criminal prosecution, recovery costs, and director liability. Failure to submit required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally based on the higher of 0.5% of undocumented transactions or 5% of reassessed profits or transactions, subject to statutory minimums and maximums.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax is generally imposed on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. The rate may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. The French parent-subsidiary exemption generally requires at least a 5% qualifying holding, a minimum holding period or commitment, and satisfaction of anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the recipient's tax authority and complete the applicable French forms, normally Form 5000 for residence certification together with Form 5001 for dividends, Form 5002 for interest, or Form 5003 for royalties, as applicable. For relief at source, provide the certified forms to the French payer or withholding agent before payment and retain beneficial-owner evidence, ownership-period evidence, treaty entitlement analysis, and anti-abuse support. If relief at source was not applied, file a refund claim with the French tax administration within the applicable statutory limitation period. Treaty benefits remain subject to principal-purpose, beneficial-ownership, anti-conduit, and domestic anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and potential EU rules. Interest paid by a French borrower to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to non-cooperative or non-cooperating jurisdictions, anti-abuse situations, or specific regulated instruments. Payments to jurisdictions on the French non-cooperative list may be subject to a 75% rate for relevant categories. Treaty rates must be verified by payment type, recipient status, beneficial ownership, residence, and the applicable treaty text.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory full transfer-pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity or group meets the EUR 150 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where the French entity is owned or controlled by an entity meeting that threshold, subject to statutory conditions. A French entity may also be required to maintain documentation for controlled transactions below that threshold, and simplified documentation or annual reporting can apply, including where annual turnover or gross assets reach EUR 50 million or where statutory related-party reporting thresholds are met. There is no general safe harbor based solely on the EUR 50,000 value of an individual transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless relevant under French transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership analysis, EU anti-avoidance rules, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, treaty principal-purpose testing, and recharacterization doctrine. The SARL should maintain real French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises appropriate to its activity, inventory and logistics evidence, commercial risk control, banking activity, accounting records, and contemporaneous evidence supporting the importation and distribution functions. A French coffee distributor should align profits with functions, assets, risks, inventory ownership, credit risk, foreign-exchange risk, and market-development activity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.sector_specific_tp_controls: For imported specialty green coffee, benchmark the purchase price and distribution remuneration using reliable product specifications, origin, grade, certification, shipment terms, lot size, quality differentials, freight, insurance, customs valuation, currency, harvest timing, and market conditions. Related-party purchases must be reconciled to customs declarations and commercial invoices. Artificially inflated purchase prices, management charges, royalties, financing costs, or year-end adjustments can create both transfer-pricing and customs valuation exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing sales, understating inventory, fabricating purchase invoices, deducting private expenses, manipulating transfer prices, or falsely claiming tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, 40% penalty for deliberate breach, 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive fraud, and criminal prosecution. Tax fraud can carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases reaching seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur personal criminal liability where they personally participated in the offense. Courts may impose confiscation, professional prohibitions, director-management restrictions, and judicial travel restrictions. The tax administration may also pursue a director whose serious and repeated misconduct made recovery from the company impossible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, fictitious residence, or permanent-establishment concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SARL with no genuine operations, routing sales or purchasing through an entity lacking substance, concealing the foreign parent's effective management, or falsely claiming that French activities are conducted outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate income tax, VAT, payroll-tax, customs, and withholding-tax reassessments; anti-abuse recharacterization; penalties of up to 80% in fraudulent cases; and potential criminal tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for intentional participation, fraudulent management, or failure to maintain required records. Criminal measures can include imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans, and judicial travel restrictions. Civil liability may include restitution of tax losses and damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for green coffee, unexplained royalty or management-fee charges, debt without commercial rationale, or failing to provide local-file, master-file, or annual reporting documentation when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustment, withholding-tax exposure, interest, penalties, and a documentation penalty generally calculated by reference to undocumented transaction amounts or reassessed profits, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Customs authorities may separately adjust import values.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for deliberate concealment, false accounting, or fraudulent documentation. Ordinary assessment generally remains a company liability, but serious managerial misconduct can support personal recovery actions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT carousel, false invoicing, or customs fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming input VAT on fictitious invoices, misdescribing coffee origin or value, under-declaring customs value, using false commodity documentation, or participating in circular transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT and customs reassessment, seizure, interest, penalties that can reach 80% for fraudulent conduct, customs fines and confiscation, and criminal prosecution. False invoices and organized VAT fraud can produce substantially higher criminal penalties under applicable circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners involved in the scheme may be prosecuted personally, face confiscation and imprisonment, and be subject to management prohibitions and judicial travel restrictions. Customs and tax authorities may seek civil recovery from responsible persons where legally available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or third-party payments, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring suspicious trade-based money laundering indicators, or falsifying source-of-funds records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory reporting, account restrictions, asset freezing, confiscation, administrative sanctions, and criminal money-laundering liability. Money laundering may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine; aggravated money laundering may carry up to ten years' imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and beneficial owners may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation or facilitation. Conviction can lead to imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans, judicial supervision, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a sanctioned supplier, bank, intermediary, or beneficial owner; concealing ownership; or structuring payments to evade EU or French restrictive measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment blocking, asset freezing, administrative and criminal penalties, confiscation, and possible imprisonment under applicable French and EU sanctions legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly authorized or facilitated the breach. Personal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, management bans, and judicial travel restrictions may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting, corporate-record, and beneficial-owner filing violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to keep reliable accounts, backdating records, destroying invoices, omitting the beneficial owner, or filing materially false annual accounts or corporate information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil and criminal penalties, refusal or loss of tax deductions, tax reassessment, accounting sanctions, and potential insolvency-related liability. Fraudulent accounting and misuse of company assets may trigger imprisonment and fines under French commercial and criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally liable for misuse of corporate assets, fraudulent accounting, serious management faults, and contribution to an insufficient insolvency estate. Courts may impose personal bankruptcy or management prohibitions, civil restitution, confiscation, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper profit distribution and shareholder extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, disguising shareholder withdrawals as expenses or loans, paying related parties without services, or bypassing withholding-tax obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, corporate-tax and withholding-tax reassessment, penalties, interest, and potential misuse-of-company-assets or fraudulent-management prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving unlawful distributions may face personal civil restitution, shareholder and creditor claims, criminal liability for misuse of company assets, management bans, confiscation, and in serious cases imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to trade while insolvent, preferring related parties, transferring assets to the foreign parent, or delaying a required insolvency filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court-supervised insolvency proceedings, clawback of transactions, director contribution to liabilities, bankruptcy restrictions, and criminal or commercial sanctions for fraudulent insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to contribute to all or part of the insufficient assets and may receive personal bankruptcy or management prohibitions. Fraudulent conduct can result in imprisonment, fines, confiscation, civil restitution, and judicial travel restrictions.
